name: DroidFinestra
author: hamed7ir
description: DroidFinestra lets you use your Android phone from Windows. It's a GUI for scrcpy, so you can see and control the phone over USB or Wi-Fi. You keep a profile for each phone (there are ready presets for the Surface RT), it builds the scrcpy command for you, pairs phones over Wi-Fi and shows scrcpy's output. This package has scrcpy, adb and FFmpeg built for 32-bit ARM Windows (scrcpy-rt, adb-rt, ffmpeg-rt), and it runs on Windows RT 8.0 and 8.1 and Windows 10 ARM32. It only needs .NET Framework 4.0, which Windows RT already has. DroidFinestra starts scrcpy but doesn't change it. scrcpy is made by Genymobile.
dependencies: .NET Framework 4.0 or newer. Windows 8 and Windows RT already have it.
USB debugging turned on, on the Android phone.
instructionSteps: On Windows RT, jailbreak the device first. RT only runs unsigned desktop apps after a jailbreak.
Run the installer. It installs for your user only into %LocalAppData%\Programs\DroidFinestra and doesn't need admin. It checks the requirements first and tells you if something is missing.
The files are not signed, so SmartScreen warns the first time. Click More info, then Run anyway.
On the phone, turn on USB debugging (in Developer options), connect it by USB and accept the USB debugging prompt on the phone.
In DroidFinestra choose New profile, start from a preset and press Launch. You see the scrcpy command line first, then scrcpy's live output.

For Wi-Fi: on the phone open Wireless debugging and choose Pair device with pairing code. In DroidFinestra open the menu, choose Pair a phone over Wi-Fi, and type the pairing address and code, then the connect address. You type the addresses, they are not found automatically.
Keep --render-driver=direct3d on. Every preset has it, and without it the scrcpy window is black on Tegra 3 tablets like the Surface RT.
